script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. November 5th already. Can you believe it?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう11月5日ですよ。信じられます？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Morning, Alex. Yeah, it is. Looks like rain today.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。うん、そうね。今日は雨みたいね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, it's definitely raining. I just ran in. My coffee almost got soaked.
script.ja: ああ、間違いなく雨ですよ。走って入ってきたばかりで。コーヒーが危うく濡れるところでした。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Forecast says moderate rain all day. High of 16.5, low 10.9. Hundred percent chance.
script.ja: 予報では一日中、並の雨みたいよ。最高気温16.5度、最低10.9度。降水確率100パーセント。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: A hundred percent? Wow. My shoes are already drenched. Need more coffee to forget about it.
script.ja: 100パーセントですか？わあ。もう靴がびしょ濡れです。忘れるためにコーヒーをもう一杯飲まないと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I saw something in the news about private high school fees. Said they almost doubled.
script.ja: ニュースで私立高校の施設費について見たわ。ほぼ倍になったって。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? That's... a lot. I wonder how families manage that.
script.ja: ああ、そうなんですか？それは…大変ですね。家族はどうやってやりくりするんだろう。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's expensive. My son's getting close to high school age, actually. Feels like everything keeps going up.
script.ja: 高いわよね。うちの息子もそろそろ高校生になる年齢なのよ。何もかも値上がりしている気がするわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, it's like these costs are just... I don't know, *entrenched* now. Like, they're just part of the system forever.
script.ja: ええ、こういう費用って、もう…なんて言うか、*entrenched*（根付いてる）って感じですよね。もうずっとシステムの一部になってる、みたいな。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: "Entrenched" means something is firmly established and hard to change.
script.ja: 「Entrenched」は、しっかりと確立されていて、変えるのが難しい、ってことよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Exactly. Hard to change. That's not going to change at my office, either. Always the same budget talk.
script.ja: まさにそれです。変えられない。うちの会社でも、それは変わりませんね。いつも同じ予算の話ばかり。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My sleep has been a bit *tenuous* lately. The baby's cutting a new tooth, I think.
script.ja: 最近、僕の睡眠はちょっと*tenuous*（不安定）なんですよ。赤ちゃんが新しい歯が生えてきてるみたいで。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Ah. That's a rough time.
script.ja: あら。それは大変な時期ね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, it is. Every little sound, I'm up. It makes you jump at everything these days.
script.ja: ええ、そうなんです。ちょっとした物音でも起きちゃって。最近は何にでもびっくりしちゃいます。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: NHK World also had a piece about Yuki Tsumugi. From Tochigi Prefecture. That unique silk manufacturing.
script.ja: NHKワールドで、結城紬についても記事が出てたわね。栃木県の。あの独特の絹織物よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that. Is that like, a famous traditional craft?
script.ja: へえ、それは知りませんでした。有名な伝統工芸品みたいなものですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. Very delicate, and takes a long time to make.
script.ja: そうよ。とても繊細で、作るのに時間がかかるの。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I always imagine those things have a lot of... like, *pomp* around them. Very formal.
script.ja: そういうものって、いつもたくさんの…なんて言うか、*pomp*（華美さ）があるって想像しちゃいます。すごくフォーマルな感じで。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: "Pomp" is more about showiness or grand ceremonies. For Yuki Tsumugi, it's more about tradition and skill. No big parades for it, usually.
script.ja: 「Pomp」は、もっと派手な見せ物とか、盛大な式典のことよ。結城紬の場合は、伝統と技術が大事で。派手なパレードがあるわけじゃないわね、普通は。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, okay. Like a... quiet elegance, then? Not like a rock concert.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。じゃあ…静かな気品、みたいな感じですか？ロックコンサートとは違う。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Exactly.
script.ja: その通りよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Did you see that Gucci owl fan? The one that's super expensive?
script.ja: あのグッチのフクロウの扇子、見ました？めちゃくちゃ高いやつ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. It was... an owl.
script.ja: 見たわ。あれは…フクロウだったわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It's kind of cute! But then I saw the price. Who buys a fan for that much money? I'm still buying my shirts on sale.
script.ja: ちょっと可愛いんですよ！でも値段見て。誰があんな高い扇子買うんですか？僕はいまだにセールでシャツ買ってますよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Well, some people do.
script.ja: まあ、買う人もいるんでしょうね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: My wife would probably just laugh if I showed her that. Maybe for a birthday, I don't know. No, definitely not.
script.ja: 妻に見せたら、たぶん笑われるだけでしょうね。誕生日とかに、どうかな。いや、絶対なしだ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Anyway, today is いいりんごの日.
script.ja: ところで、今日は「いいりんごの日」よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, really? いいりんご? Is that "good apple day"?
script.ja: ああ、そうなんですか？いいりんご？「良いりんごの日」ってことですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. November 5th. It's because "ii" sounds like 1-1, and "ringo" for 5. As in 11/5.
script.ja: そうよ。11月5日。「いい」が11で、「りんご」が5。11月5日、ってわけね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: That's clever. I like apples. My kid just started mashing them up and eating them. It's a mess. But progress!
script.ja: それは面白いですね。僕はりんご好きですよ。うちの子も、最近りんごを潰して食べ始めたんです。めちゃくちゃになるけど。でも進歩だ！

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Sounds like it. My daughter loves apples too. Always has.
script.ja: そうみたいね。うちの娘もりんご大好きよ。昔からずっと。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Well, that's what's happening today on The Daily Tanu-chan Show. Or at least what Alex and Sarah are talking about.
script.ja: さて、今日は「ザ・デイリー・タヌちゃんショー」で、こんな話をしていましたね。というか、アレックスとサラが話していた内容です。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yeah.
script.ja: うん。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I really do need more coffee. Maybe a rain jacket next time.
script.ja: 本当にコーヒーもう一杯必要です。次はレインジャケット着てこようかな。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You probably do. I'm going to refill my tea.
script.ja: そうした方がいいかもね。私はお茶を入れ直してくるわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Sounds good. We'll be back tomorrow.
script.ja: いいですね。また明日。
